paper.title: From Linear to Linearizable Optimization: A Novel Framework with Applications to Stationary and Non-stationary DR-submodular Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Online linear maximization with deterministic gradient oracle, fully adaptive adversary
settings.definition_quote: Let $\BF{L}$ be a class of linear functions over $\C{K}$ such that $\|l\| \leq M_1$ for all $l \in \BF{L}$ and let $D = \op{diam}(\C{K})$.

settings.name_in_paper: Monotone up-concave maximization over general convex sets, deterministic semi-bandit (first-order) feedback, fully adaptive adversary
unmapped: rewards are non-negative monotone mu-strongly gamma-weakly up-concave functions (generalizing gamma-weakly DR-submodular) w.r.t. a specified up-super-gradient field, with curvature at most c, extendable to [0,1]^d; K subset of [0,1]^d
approximation ratio alpha = gamma^2/(1+c*gamma^2)
settings.definition_quote: let $\BF{F}$ be an $M_1$-Lipschitz function class over $\C{K}$ where every $f \in \BF{F}$ admits a non-negative continuous monotone extension $\bar f : [0,1]^d \to \B{R}$ with curvature bounded by $c$ that is $\mu$-strongly $\gamma$-weakly up-concave with respect to a specified vector-valued function

settings.name_in_paper: Monotone up-concave maximization over general convex sets, stochastic semi-bandit feedback, oblivious adversary

stochastic unbiased gradient oracle with outputs bounded in norm by B_1
approximation ratio alpha = gamma^2/(1+c*gamma^2)
settings.definition_quote: For the stochastic bound, the oracle is an unbiased estimator of this same field on $\C{K}$, with outputs bounded by $B_1$.

settings.name_in_paper: Monotone up-concave maximization over general convex sets, deterministic zeroth-order full-information (two-point) feedback, oblivious adversary

two value queries per round at points near (not equal to) the played point
approximation ratio alpha = gamma^2/(1+c*gamma^2)
settings.definition_quote: Query the deterministic oracle at the points $T_\delta(\y_{t, i}) + \delta \vv_{t, i}$ and $T_\delta(\y_{t, i}) - \delta \vv_{t, i}$
